blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a EuroSys 2016 paper that explores the performance and cost implications of integrating non-volatile memory (NVM) into existing systems, particularly in-memory datastores like MemC3, VoltDB, and GraphMat. The paper demonstrates that using a small fraction of DRAM (6-25% of total memory) alongside NVM can achieve performance only 13-40% worse than all-DRAM systems while offering 2x to 2.8x better performance per dollar. The key insight is intelligent data structure placement: without careful optimization (enabled by the X-Mem system), performance can degrade by 1.5x to 5.9x. The paper also provides a cost-benefit analysis of hybrid DRAM-NVM configurations, showing tradeoffs between performance, cost, and memory tiering ratios. X-Mem, a runtime system, profiles applications to determine optimal placement of data structures in DRAM or NVM, significantly improving performance in hybrid systems.
paper_title: Data Tiering in Heterogeneous Memory Systems
